findings.text: The issue requires this and the change does not meet it: RQTIE-1: The arbitration code exists in plugin.sh, but no assertion in `plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh` or `tests/e2e/claim-race-test.sh` covers the gh-backend concurrent-claim path. Removing the arbitration logic would leave all current tests green. — plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh | print_test_header "plugin: claim-coordinator/github-labels — claim and release" — ACCEPTED IF: When two runs claim an issue at the same moment, exactly one proceeds

The issue requires this and the change does not meet it: RQREB-1: `_ccgl_read_labels "$issue" || true` is called after the note post, but no test asserts that the re-read happens after the synchronous write. Deleting that call leaves every test green. — plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh | _ccgl_read_labels "$issue" || true — ACCEPTED IF: After adding the label, a run re-reads the issue

The issue requires this and the change does not meet it: RQTIE-2: `_ccgl_race_note_first_v` selects the winner by `created_at` then `id`, and the loser path returns `race_lost: true`, but no test asserts that the first-note-wins rule is enforced. No DSRACE-2 assertion exists in any named test file. — plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh | if [[ -z "$winner" || "$winner" == "$my_holder" ]]; then — ACCEPTED IF: If another run claimed it too, the run that claimed first wins

The issue requires this and the change does not meet it: RQCMT-1: `_ccgl_race_note_update` PATCHes the losing note to "not started — concurrent claim: `<winner>` was first", but no test asserts this PATCH happens. No DSRACE-3 assertion exists in any named test file. — plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh | _ccgl_race_note_update "$note_id" "$_CCGL_SLUG" "$issue" "$winner" || true — ACCEPTED IF: The later run marks its progress comment as not started

The issue requires this and the change does not meet it: RQLBL-1: When `race_lost: true`, `claim.sh` returns 1 without setting `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED`, so `zbuild_claim_release` does not remove the label. The behaviour is coded, but no DSRACE-4 assertion exists in any named test file. Removing the `race_lost` branch leaves all tests green. — core/claim/claim.sh | if [[ "$reply" =~ \"race_lost\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true ]]; then — ACCEPTED IF: The later run exits without removing the label

The issue requires this and the change does not meet it: RQTIE-3: `_ccgl_race_note_post_v` is called synchronously before `_ccgl_read_labels`, satisfying the requirement in code, but no test asserts the ordering (DSRACE-1 or DSRACE-7). Swapping or removing the synchronous write leaves all tests green. — plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh | _ccgl_race_note_post_v note_id "$_CCGL_SLUG" "$issue" "$my_holder" || note_rc=$? — ACCEPTED IF: Either the claim writes its holder record itself, synchronously, before it re-reads, or the tie-break uses something that exists at claim time
